title: Metal: Ensure baked Metal binaries can be loaded on the minimum target OS
body:
Closes #109846

# Summary

Ensure baked Metal binaries can be loaded on the minimum target OS for the exported Apple platform.

Supersedes:

- #110244

> [!NOTE]
>
> This PR incorporates PR #110244 to specify the `<os>-version-min` argument, but performs additional runtime checks to ensure the shader can be loaded by the target OS. Further, it uses the Metal toolchain to provide details about the target OS and Metal shader language to ensure SPIR-V → Metal succeeds by not enabling features that may be unavailable for the target OS.

# Background

Originally, #109846 reported that baked shaders would not load due to the target OS (iOS 17.x) Metal language being lower than the `.metallib` binary being loaded:

```text
drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal.mm:2435:compute_pipeline_create(): error creating pipeline: Function main0 is using language version 3.2 which is incompatible with this OS. Condition "error != nullptr" is true. Returning: PipelineID()
```

The first fix, #110063, attempted to address that by setting the default minimum Metal version to 3.1, which is available on iOS 17.x and the device being validate per [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109846#issuecomment-3229210794):

```
Metal 3.1 - Forward Mobile - Using Device #0: Apple - Apple A15 GPU (Apple8)
```

This change succeeded in suppressing the error; however, a new issue surfaced regarding an incompatibility with the `.metallib` being loaded per [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109846#issuecomment-3250099771):

```text
drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal.mm:2440:compute_pipeline_create(): error creating pipeline: Function main0 has a deployment target (0x00020007) which is incompatible with this OS (0x00020006). Condition "error != nullptr" is true. Returning: PipelineID()
```

This second issue was due to the compilation logic not specifying the `<os>-version-min` argument to the Metal compiler toolchain, thus using the toolchain default, which for Xcode 16 would be iOS 18:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3c7f9b937214068bc892be0d2bd9a8a7026edae1/drivers/metal/rendering_shader_container_metal.mm#L118-L127

@TCROC discovered this and introduced PR #110244 to address this. This PR incorporated those changes and added these additional changes:

## Determine OS and Metal language from toolchain

To ensure the generated SPIR-V targets the correct Metal language, the Metal compiler toolchain is inspected to extract some preprocessor variables, essentially running and parsing the following:

```sh
echo "" | xcrun -sdk iphoneos metal -mios-version-min=17.0 -E -dM -x metal - | grep -E "__METAL_VERSION__|__ENVIRONMENT_OS"
```
```
#define __ENVIRONMENT_OS_VERSION_MIN_REQUIRED__ 170000
#define __METAL_VERSION__ 310
```

Here we can see that targeting iOS 17 uses the Metal 310 or 3.1 language standard. The shader baker parses this and ensures SPIRV-Cross generates Metal source for Metal 3.1 and then executes the compiler toolchain with the same arguments.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> This override only takes place when baking shaders. Under normal conditions, recompiling shaders will target the highest Metal language standard available on the target device.

## Perform runtime checks in the Metal driver

At runtime in the [`shader_create_from_container`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3c7f9b937214068bc892be0d2bd9a8a7026edae1/drivers/metal/rendering_device_driver_metal.mm#L1126) function, further checks are performed to ensure the baked shader can be loaded.
